shared_elements: large upright freestanding carved stone monolith
shallow low-relief carving on the broad face
a distinct upper zone/block with a row of repeated small motifs along the top edge
horizontal dividing band or register separating upper from lower field
curved arm-like or crescentic bands descending on the body
small schematic animal or figural forms in relief
rounded circular or loop element within the main field
justification: Both are tall upright stone blocks whose broad face is organised the same way: a wide upper zone carrying a row of repeated small motifs, a horizontal dividing band beneath it, then a large field with schematic creatures, curved arm-like bands and chevron hatching running down the shaft. The clearest difference is the handling and stone: A is dark, heavily weathered and modelled in plump rounded volumes with prominent discs and a sculpted head-like cap, whereas B is pale, flat-faced and cut in crisp thin linear relief with an explicit T-shaped projecting top, so a common hand or workshop is not credible.
